## Sequencing and ownership

The [space and interaction plan](/home/yan/src/quod/nimbalyst-local/plans/space-conceptual-architecture-review.md) is authoritative. [stage 2](/home/yan/src/quod/nimbalyst-local/tracker/tasks.md:42) owns shared space/Eidolon opening, recursive ontology-content integration and access to the guarded source editor. This ticket consumes that delivery and tracks only the remaining bounded graphical workbench application: class/instance/relation presentation and convenient authorized creation/edit/deletion. Do not implement shared view plumbing or the source editor twice. Acceptance already demonstrated by stage 2 is reused with its evidence.

This ticket remains unstarted and depends on stage 2 in addition to its completed ontology-reflection foundation. It does not block stage 1 or stage 2, reopen their settled decisions, or expand the three normalization stages with a universal graphical editor.

## Goal
Let an authorized user see, interact with, edit and build ontology contents in 3D using existing lenses, encodings, Eidolons, marks and owner-authorized actions. Quod is not limited to walking through physical rooms.

## Scope
- Supply a bounded first 3D workbench for ontology contents: show classes, instances and selected relations; select exact anchored targets; inspect them and perform authorized creation/edit/deletion through existing action/editing owners. Define the first supported operations explicitly rather than promising a universal graphical Prolog editor.
- A class-diagram view, 3D workbench, text editor and ACL view are presentations of the same ontology. Switching or opening multiple representations does not clone its ontology, source or history. Ontologies themselves are ordinary class instances with Eidolons and marks.
- Reuse lens selection versus encoding/representation separation; do not impose an independent client filter or new presentation engine. Generalize the existing dispatcher as needed rather than treating all Eidolons as code forms.
- Distinguish presentation layout from actual domain edits. Moving a mark for readability does not move ownership or a physical body. Explicit domain edits use the target ACLs and expected state; correlated durable edits use existing atomic transactions.
- The agreed model makes ontology a specialized space of predicates. Displaying an Eidolon does not create a new containing-space assignment, physical_space membership, simulation or collision geometry. Nonphysical ontologies remain usable without a physics service.

## Acceptance
On a system read-only ontology and an owned non-lobby ontology, visualize coherent current content, inspect class/instance identity, create/edit/delete within granted policy and see the same committed result in the text view. Test denial, wrong anchor, concurrent edit, deleted targets, revocation and reconnect/uncertain outcomes. Local layout cannot mutate domain location. Repeated unchanged views do not replay history or rebuild retained state.

Reuse [QUD.25](nimbalyst://QUD.25)'s common GUI infrastructure where available; this ticket owns the ontology-editing application, not the general form/question lifecycle. The dedicated text Eidolon is a sibling consumer, not a second source of truth. Hardware VR interaction validation must be recorded separately from desktop/rendering checks.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md and doc/multiwrite-architecture.md before implementation. Reuse existing Prolog policy/actions, lifecycle, recovery and authorized owner paths. No parallel domain engine, hidden fallback or backward-compatibility branch. Clean replacement does not authorize deployment, refounding or history deletion.

Ordinary ontology-instance dispatch/ACL reflection: [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32). Highlighted text editing: [QUD.34](nimbalyst://QUD.34). Any actual space containment action uses the shared placement/entry path normalized in stages 1/2 from [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33), rather than inferring location from mark layout."}
